text:
中国小伙在意大利街头迷路，随口问了个18岁女孩，后来把人娶回了中国

2015年，一个中国小伙去意大利旅游，在威尼斯彻底迷路了。

手机导航转了快两个小时，衣服都被汗湿透，愣是没找到提前订好的旅馆。

正发愁时，他看见路边坐着一个姑娘。

一米七五左右，长得特别漂亮。

他硬着头皮，用散装英语问路。

姑娘听完不仅告诉他怎么走，还主动提出带他过去。

一路聊天才知道，对方叫柏妮，刚满18岁，是个刚入行的意大利模特。

到了旅馆，两人互留了联系方式。

原本只是一场问路。

后来小伙回国，两人却一直保持联系，从聊天到恋爱，再到跨国奔现。

最后，这个当年在威尼斯连酒店都找不到的中国游客，直接把当初给自己带路的意大利姑娘娶回了中国。

后来朋友问他：

“你这辈子做过最赚的一件事是什么？”

他想都没想：

“2015年在威尼斯迷路。”

有时候导航把你带错路，

可能只是它觉得——

你订的那个酒店，哪有老婆重要。

text:
chatgpt plus $20 刀套餐生存建议..

1. 每天早上6点给自己发消息.  

Work里设置 "请每天UTC+8 6am 给自己发送一个 'Good morning' 的消息 "

这是因为现在 plus套餐又有了5小时窗口了. 它是从每天第一条消息开始算的. 也就是你这样设置后, 大概上午11点就会重置5小时窗口. 你刚好干活1-2小时.  重置后可以续上.

2.善用 ChatGPT Chat(聊天)
chat的 token额度和 work/codex编码额度是分开的. 而且给的非常充足,  选5.6 sol high一个月估计可以用出来 300$-400$

所以对于以前在codex用 /plan 做的规划, 可以直接把核心代码项目拖到 chat窗口里, 让它探索, 制定规划.

比较适合的就是一些宏观角度的问题.  比如说 "我有两个xxx组件,某个yyy工程问题, 可以怎么处理"

不太适合已有项目一大堆代码来debug, 或者做代码implement.  (网页里面给你生成一大堆代码你复制过来也很麻烦)

3. 限制使用模型 

看你具体情况.  可以  
/plan  --> 5.6 sol high  
代码生成 --> 5.6 sol medium  
debug和review --> 5.6 sol high

如果token捉襟见肘, 或者项目本身不复杂, 可以 
/plan 5.6 --> medium 
代码生成 --> Luna high
debug和review --> 5.6 sol medium

这不能证明“codex用view picture来读docx”，

只能证明“当前codex版本，用当前的model，配上当前的skills和plugins，在当前的任务下，以当前的random seed启动的inference下，选择了用view picture来读docx”。

我从来不观察它工作的原因，是因为我知道它干的一定不是最优解，它自己会调整，

人类如果强行去观察和介入agent工作方式，无异于一个天天盯着你电脑看的老板，非常微管理且没有意义，只能打断别人且惹人烦。

他一个人吭哧吭哧拆了半天，最后一趟搬完的时候，整个人已经快散架了。

临走前，他和卖家一人买了一瓶冰红茶，坐那儿咕咚咕咚喝。

这时候他终于明白了：

为什么闲鱼上那么多家具只支持自提。

那1块钱不是床钱。

是卖家花1块钱，雇了个人来家里帮忙拆床、搬床，最后还不用处理旧家具。

text:
刘翔为什么不满？23年，被分走的广告费可能过亿

退役11年，安置没来。8月26日，刘翔被逼二选一：买断走人，还是回体制当教练。

他回怼上海有关部门：“十年了想起来安置我了，分广告费的时候怎么不依法依规安置我。”

广告费怎么分的？

2008年之前—“5122”模式：

刘翔本人：50%

教练孙海平及保障团队：15%

上海体育局（输送单位）：20%

田管中心（中国田协）：15%

-

2008年之后—运动员比例上调：

刘翔本人：65%

教练及团队：15%

上海体育局：10%

田管中心：10%

巅峰期每赚100块，35到50块分给了别人。

接了多少广告？

巅峰期同时手握20多个代言，单笔最高1500万/年，退役后还有耐克终身合同，年入约1400万。在役11年，商业总收入约5.35亿。

被分走多少？（推算，仅供参考）

按分配比例算：上海体育局约1.07亿，田协约8000万，合计约1.87亿。

更关键的是：有知情人透露，只要编制挂着，退役后的广告收入还要返点约20%。这11年，安置没影，分成没停。

分钱的时候按规办事，安置的时候规没了。刘翔怒的，就是这个。

文中金额为媒体推算，未经官方核实，仅供参考。

那个曾经在白银94美元时喊出120美元目标、6月中又精准抄底黄金的神奇分析师AG Thorson，再次发表观点，比特币已于8.25触顶：

他认为，黄金从中期底部反弹以来已经上涨接近20%，短期随时可能迎来一至两周的回调。

我记得托尔森最神的一次，就是提前预判白银会冲向120美元，随后暴跌30%至50%。
后来白银最高涨到121.67美元，紧接着真的出现了超过30%的快速回撤，战绩可查。

关于回调什么时候真正开始？他给出的确认信号是：黄金连续收在4500美元下方。

不过托尔森长期依然看好白银，会调结束后，极端行情下会再次冲击120至140美元。

关于比特币就有意思了：
短期还有最后一冲，中期仍然看空，预计9月至10月出现最后一轮洗盘。
他的判断是：
这轮上涨更像熊市里的“最后一拉”
短期周期可能在8月25日至26日前后见顶（目前确实是一个小高点）
随后可能跌破5万美元
极端目标接近4万美元
最终在10月附近形成四年周期底部

João Palhinha is still a top player with a great character, who has clear strengths. But not the way that perfectly fits our midfield. Of course when a player costs a lot of money and doesn't work out, people quickly talk about a flop - but there was a factual reason for that. 本地高强度跑完 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 和 GLM-5.3-FLASH，一个极其恐怖的事实已经摆在台面上了：

1 到 2 台 DGX Spark，或者一台顶配 Mac Studio，现在已经能把接近前沿梯队的 AI 能力焊死在本地。

用起来的体感不仅远超被暗中砍废的 Opus-5，甚至能稳稳咬住没挨刀之前的 Opus-4.8。

这件事最致命的地方，是它直接击碎了闭源巨头赖以生存的护城河。

OpenAI、Anthropic 这帮硅谷大厂，最核心的商业逻辑就是用高昂的订阅费和 API 价格，把开发者死死锁在自家的云端算力机房里。为了保住毛利，它们在后台偷偷搞隐蔽降级（Stealth Nerfing）、砍推理深度、塞安全废话，赌的就是你在本地根本没有替代方案。

结果开源生态用极致的架构压缩和量化刀法，直接在消费级和边缘硬件上完成了降维偷袭。

当开发者发现一台本地硬件就能吃下代码重构、长上下文和复杂 Agent 任务，而且没有调用限流、没有审查打断、没有后台偷偷降级的时候，谁还会每个月给云端 API 上贡？

这是一场正在发生的算力逃离。

如果硅谷大厂还不赶紧把压仓的 Astra 和下一代 Fable 掏出来打明牌，闭源高溢价的泡沫很快就会被本地端侧算力戳得千疮百孔。

巨头还在打着算盘怎么在云端抠成本。

开发者已经把前沿智能搬进自己的机箱，准备随时拔掉网线了。

text:
一张加床，让62岁的影帝梁家辉和女儿在镜头前吵了起来。女儿Chloe怕他腰疼，他怕麻烦别人；两个人都在心疼对方，出口却全成了火药。

2019年录制《一路成年》时，父女三人住进一间只有一张床的酒店房间。两个女儿决定把床让给父亲，自己睡沙发或加床。梁家辉却抢先坐上沙发，坚持自己将就一晚。

大女儿Chloe知道他背部不舒服，反复要求酒店加床。梁家辉嫌麻烦，回了一句：“你管我。” Chloe瞬间炸了：“叫他们加张床有多难？这里是酒店。”两个人越说越硬，最后女儿气得转身离开。

事后，梁家辉解释，他只是想把舒服的床留给女儿；女儿也说，她无法看着父亲明明身体不适还硬扛。这场争执没有谁自私，恰恰相反，是两个人都太习惯用牺牲证明爱。

很多父母只会付出，却不会接受。他们以为“我能扛”是在疼孩子，却忘了孩子长大后，也需要拥有照顾父母的权利。

不过这种“吵架”蕴含着真挚亲情的爱，试问多少人想要而不得啊！

text:
前几天，同事孩子生病了，她向我借了我5万块元。今天发了工资，把钱转给了我。 当我看到只有5万元整的时候，我有点无语。

我说：“我借给你的是5万元，这么多天了，多少应该有点利息的吧”

同事听了我的话，脸上露出了一丝尴尬，连忙说道：“哎呀，不好意思，我还真没想到这利息的事儿，您看多少合适，我马上补给你。”

我看着她有些慌张的神情，心中不禁软了下来。其实，我并不是真的在乎那一点利息，只是我觉得这是一种人与人之间交往的基本规则和礼貌。但看到她如此反应，我也不想太过苛刻。 

我略一沉思，然后说道：“这样吧，你也不用太在意，利息就给200元吧，算是意思一下。” 

同事显然没想到我会这么说，她愣了一下，然后连忙感激地说道：“谢谢你，这样我有信心，下个月一定还给你。” 

我笑了笑，说道：“没关系，谁都有个难处的时候。孩子现在好点了吗？” 

她听到我问起孩子，脸上露出了温柔的笑容，“好多了，谢谢你的关心。” 

我们两人又聊了一会儿，然后各自回到了自己的工作岗位。

其实，人与人之间的相处，有时候并不需要太过计较。一点小小的让步，也许就能换来更加和谐。

text:
Proprietary AI is getting speedrun in real time.

Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B A6B MoE) on the Artificial Analysis Agentic Index: 

- Beats Kimi 3 (Max)  
- Sitting just 1 point behind Claude Fable 5 
- Hardware: Single RTX 3090 / 4090 (24GB VRAM) + 100GB RAM

Matching top tier API performance on a single consumer GPU setup is insane.

Open weights are moving absurdly fast. Are you still paying top dollar for closed APIs or self hosting?

quotedTweet.text:
The VRAM barrier is officially dead.

I just ran Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (MoE) 125B A6B with a  250,000 context window on a single 24GB RTX 4090.

21 tokens/sec decode. 364 t/s prefill. 

no mtp. no dflash. no kv cache quantization!

We are running datacenter models on consumer hardware.

Tested on Ubuntu 22 | CUDA 13.0 | PCIe 4.0 x16 | 110 GB DDR4 System RAM with a continuous 28k prompt across all runs.

### The Benchmarks & Scaling

# 1. Hybrid Offload (-ncmoe 40 @ 80k Context)
Offloaded 40 expert layers to the GPU, pushing VRAM to the ceiling.

./build/bin/llama-server -m Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf -c 80000 --port 8080 -v --fit off -b 4096 -ub 4096 -ncmoe 40

Prefill: 383.85 t/s | Decode: 22.52 t/s
Footprint: 23.85 GB VRAM | 97 GB RAM

# 2. Full CPU MoE Offload (-cmoe @ 80k Context)

Pinned all 512 expert layers to DDR4 RAM (-cmoe), keeping attention on the 4090.

llama.cpp flags: (Same as above, replace -ncmoe 40 with -cmoe)

Prefill: 355.72 t/s | Decode: 20.84 t/s
Footprint: 11.66 GB VRAM (12GB+ VRAM freed up!) | 110 GB RAM

# 3. The 180,000 Context Run

Prefill: 357.75 t/s | Decode: 20.98 t/s | VRAM: 15.6 GB | RAM: 110 GB

# 4. The 250,000 Context Absolute Ceiling

./build/bin/llama-server -m Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf -c 250000 --port 8080 -v --fit off -b 4096 -ub 4096 -cmoe

Prefill: 364.29 t/s | Decode: 20.97 t/s

Footprint: 18.3 GB VRAM (Still ~5.7 GB of VRAM headroom!) | 110 GB RAM

### Key Insights:
-b 4096 -ub 4096: doubles the prompt ingestion from ~150 to 364+ t/s.
-cmoe Free Lunch: Shifting expert layers to DDR4 RAM slashes VRAM from 24GB to 11.6GB with virtually zero decode penalty (22.5 -> 20.9 t/s), enabling the 250k context ceiling.

Qwen 3.8 Flash-Next (UD-Q4_K_XL) is a massive 111.4 GB model split across 4 shards. To run this architecture, you must build from the experimental PR branch (#27742) by @danielhanchen:

git clone && cd llama.cpp 
git fetch origin pull/27742/head:qwen-next && git checkout qwen-next 
cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=native -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF 
cmake --build build --config Release -j $(nproc) --target llama-server

A single 4090 paired with 100 GB of cheap DDR4 RAM will comfortably serve production grade 125B inference.

While Qwen 3.8 27B (dense) still holds the crown for single 3090/4090 rigs, Flash Next proves 125B hybrid models are officially viable on consumer hardware. 

Hugging Face GGUF link and complete performance telemetry graphs are dropped in the replies below.

GLM 5.3 Flash VS Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, which one takes the open weights crown this week?

text:
一男子包养在校法学女硕士，六年花掉136万。被男子老婆以夫妻共同财产，起诉到法院，要求女硕士返还资金。
女硕士说，从一开始，她与男子就不是男女朋友关系，或者男女不正当关系。
她说自己是一个卖淫女，与男子是一次一结，属于卖淫嫖娼关系。
女硕士还是一个在校生，又是一个法学生，她如果说与男子是恋爱关系或者说不正当关系，都不涉嫌违法。卖淫属于违法行为，而且传出去名声也不好，她为什么强调自己是卖淫女？
这正是这个法学女硕士的厉害之处。
如果与男子属于恋爱关系或不正当关系，男子对她花掉的136万，确实属于男子的夫妻共同财产，男子老婆有权利追回，法院大概率会支持男子老婆的诉求。
但卖淫行为属于违法行为。男子的嫖资就是违法资金，公安机关应该追缴上缴国库。
但女硕士最近一次与男子的卖淫行为已经过去九个月，超过了六个月的追诉期。但违法所得没有追诉期，她获得的136万收入不还是保不住吗？
治安处理管理办法规定，卖淫收入如果被挥霍或者无法溯源，将不再追缴。
女硕士家境贫困，父亲透析九年，自己本科研究生六年，卖淫所得早已花光，公安机关无法追缴。
看了这个女孩的故事，内心五味杂陈。既为她的荒唐行为而哭笑不得，又对女孩充满同情。以她的情况看，很难将她与坏女人联系起来。
家里因父亲生病可能早已一贫如洗，自己又想完成学业。对她来说，走到卖淫这条路，恐怕也绝不是自己所愿。她唯一能用到的办法，就是用自己所学法律知识规避行政处罚。

text:
总结下孙宇晨写的景甜的瓜：

1）某女星是孙宇晨惦记了十九年的白月光。2007年，刚进入北大的孙宇晨在QQ广告中看到他，保存了她的模糊照片，还在校内网上给她发送好友申请，只写了“你好”，但她没有通过。此后十九年，无论更换多少设备，他都一直保存着这张照片。

2）孙宇晨早年生活拮据，买一件150元的羽绒服都要犹豫三天。与此同时，她已经获得《战国》《长城》等巨额投资和顶级明星资源。孙宇晨后来创业致富，曾经在赚到十亿、一百亿时想过，自己到了什么程度，她才会接受当年的好友申请。

3）十九年后，两人在瑰丽酒店第一次见面。孙宇晨发现自己没有预想中紧张，因为他见到的不只是现实中的她，也是自己幻想了十九年的白月光。之后她想看《疯狂动物城2》，要求放映厅里只能有他们两个人，孙宇晨便买下全部座位，并用现金补偿已经买票的二十六名观众。

4）两人当晚发生了亲密接触。孙宇晨用手揉她，她把他推开。孙宇晨以为她不愿意，后来她解释，是他的指甲边缘太尖，扎得她疼。她拿出磨甲工具，把孙宇晨的十根手指一根一根修磨、抛光，前后花了接近一个小时。磨完后她对他说，现在可以摸了，想摸哪里都行。

5）磨指甲时，她还说：“要是以后我不在了，就再没有人给你抛指甲了。”这句话后来成为全文的重要伏笔。她离开后，孙宇晨再次剪指甲，发现指甲还是尖的。他拿出她留下的磨甲工具，却已经忘记应该朝哪个方向磨，最后只能放回抽屉。

6）交往三个月后，孙宇晨让人调查了她的项目、公司、股权、账户、房产、家庭成员和私人关系，形成四十多页资料。她后来亲口告诉他的部分内容，与调查资料并不完全一致。孙宇晨没有拆穿她，也没有追问。他说自己全部相信她说的话，但又一个字也不信。

7）两人乘私人飞机前往特纳里费时，她主动要求孙宇晨以后不要叫名字，要叫她“妈妈”。孙宇晨答应了。这种称呼反映出两人关系中，她掌握主导权，孙宇晨则表现出明显的依赖、服从和讨好。

8）她要求周围不能有人，睡觉时不能有一丝光。孙宇晨动用私人飞机、助理、保镖和酒店人员，包场、清空楼层，用黑胶带遮住窗户、空调灯和插座灯。之后她嫌特纳里费太冷，两人又带着三十人的团队前往马尔代夫。她在那里提出和孙宇晨要一个孩子，而且必须通过代孕完成。

9）她以结婚和彩礼为由，让孙宇晨向xxx、xxx的账户转入三千万元人民币。2026年1月2日，孙宇晨在马尔代夫向她求婚，她认为钻戒太小，表示以后要补一个大的。她还多次问孙宇晨能不能来北京。孙宇晨的沉默不是因为不想去，而是因为他没有办法回中国。她此前一直在北京进行抽血、激素、B超和卵巢储备检查，为取卵做准备。

text:
你的 pi 正在用 grep 往 Context 里塞垃圾，我实测了一下午终于换掉了...

pi 内置的 grep 其实就是 rg --json 套壳，limit 100 + 截断 50KB + 默认带 --hidden，搜一次 TODO 这种高频词，直接30 多条平铺甩进上下文。Token 烧了，关键文件还被埋在后面

这个问题 Codex 早就用优化过的 rg 解决，pi 这边最干净的解法我测下来是 @ff-labs/pi-fff 

它不是再包一层 rg，而是把 FFF 这个 Rust 原生库直接接到 pi 里，不起子进程，文件在后台预索引。核心变化就三点：frecency 排序常用文件自动置顶、git-aware 改动过的文件加权、grep 结果分组 + cursor 分页

我测了一下，本地建了个小项目  src/app.ts / utils.ts / README.md，往 noise.ts 里塞了 30 行 TODO fix，总共 33 个命中

用内置逻辑等价于 rg "TODO"，33 行平铺一次性返回。换成 ffgrep：

第一页只给 20 条，全是 noise.ts 分组好的 1-20，还带一句 [Continue with cursor="fff_c1"]。第二页 ffgrep
cursor="fff_c1" 才吐剩下 13 条，app.ts 和 utils.ts 被分在后面，首屏完全不淹没

fffind 也一样，fffind pattern:"app" 直接模糊命中 src/app.ts 和 README.md，frecency 会把你最近改过的文件排前面，不用写 glob。

1️⃣ 安装就一行，不用装 rg/fd 二进制

>  pi install npm:@ff-labs/pi-fff

装完 reload 就有 ffgrep / fffind / fff-multi-grep。默认是 tools-and-ui 额外加工具，想直接替换掉内置 grep 就切
override 模式：PI_FFF_MODE=override 或启动加 --fff-mode override

2️⃣ 为什么选它不选别的
我扫了一遍 pi 插件库同期数据，@ff-labs/pi-fff 周下载 6,830 / 月 33,928，版本 0.10.5，已经 80+ 个 nightly 迭代，是搜索类最成熟的。对比 pi-lean-grep 周下载才 4，pi-hypa 是做压缩的，定位不一样。

3️⃣ 体感变化
默认 ffgrep limit 20 对比内置 100，首屏噪音直接砍掉 80%。配合 cursor，你是「精准定位再 read」，而不是「先把50KB 塞进 Context 再让模型自己找」。/fff-health 还能看索引和 frecency 状态

说真的，pi 默认 4 个工具 read,bash,edit,write 之外，grep/find 本来就得显式启用，既然要开，不如直接开这个

已经在用 pi 写代码、被 grep 刷屏搞崩过 Context 的人可以试试，尤其大仓、TODO / FIXME 满天飞的项目，提升最明显

推荐大家在pi里试试

传送门 👉 https://t.co/Q5uWHsuDWA

#pi #VibeCoding

text:
我必须说一句，福建杨梅挺冤枉的，人家实际上沾的糖精钠和脱氢乙酸钠，你可以认为几乎无毒。

我可以说，杨梅泡在这俩的溶液中，完全也是违规违法，因为你不知道是否顾客有过敏或者有特殊禁忌症，但是这俩在当代食品工业已经太正常了，实际上危害没那么大。

反而整个北方拿甲醛（福尔马林）泡白菜， 这种才是最恶劣的，因为甲醛这种物质的毒性没有最低值，无论残留多少，都会有线性概率导致癌症，因为理论上来看，这东西就是直接干你细胞DNA的。

当然，甘肃天水幼儿园铅中毒事件，我也是全网第一个全网辟谣的，告诉你们不存在垃圾处理厂的重金属泄露，完完全全就是民办三本文科宝妈灵机一动，带着工业颜料下厨房给孩子们做彩色馒头造成的傻逼奇葩行为事件。

就这几个食品安全问题排个名，甲醛白菜的恶劣程度断层第一，恶劣在这是目前食品安全系统无法防范、无法罚款、集体违规、伤害明确、法不责众、人人都吃、人人躲不开的真实案例。

我个人建议就是，在这个问题彻底解决之前，国内非山姆采购的绿叶蔬菜尽可能少吃，甚至可以完全不吃，吃个西红柿黄瓜茄子就可以了，好歹削皮了就能保证健康。

Max Eberl on Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or chances: "You have to look at the role Harry Kane has played in world football over the past few years, both at Tottenham and, especially, at Bayern Munich. For me, a Ballon d’Or winner isn’t simply about scoring the most goals or winning the most trophies. Harry can compete with anyone on both counts, except for [winning] the Champions League, so far. But above all, for me, it comes down to this: What does it mean to be a role model? If you look at Harry Kane as a footballer, both on and off the pitch, he is someone kids and society as a whole can look up to and take inspiration from in terms of how to conduct themselves.
To me, those are the qualities of an ambassador, and a Ballon d’Or winner should also be an ambassador. That’s why, for me, Harry Kane is actually the clear choice." [@SkySportDE]

text:
$NVDA 财报最被忽视的细节:  $SPCX 可能才是隐藏的大赢家。

英伟达说，合作的Neocloud到2026年底将拥有8GW已安装容量。

但公开数字暂时对不上：

CoreWeave年底超过1.85GW；
Nebius年底约0.8至1.0GW。
两家最大的上市纯Neocloud，加起来只有约2.7至2.9GW。

剩下约5GW去了哪里？

这5GW不能直接全部算给SpaceX，里面还有Nscale、Crusoe、Lambda、Fluidstack、IREN等运营商。

但SpaceX很可能藏在其中，而且规模不小。

三条官方数据已经对上：

SpaceX二季度AI名义算力达到1.4GW，一年前只有0.4GW；

同季签下141亿美元云服务合同，带来16亿美元新增AI基础设施收入；

NVDA在财报前两天宣布，SpaceXAI将使用Vera Rubin继续扩张至GW级算力，并准备把同一架构送入轨道。

这意味着SpaceX正在发生一个重要变化：

过去，它是花钱购买GPU、训练Grok的客户。

现在，它开始把这些GPU出租给Google、Anthropic等外部客户，变成AI算力运营商。

而黄仁勋在电话会上给出了一个惊人的数字：

Hopper每GW对应约180亿美元英伟达平台收入；
Grace Blackwell约250亿美元；
Vera Rubin约400亿美元。

注意：这400亿美元不是SpaceX的收入。
但它说明，SpaceX账上那1.4GW已经不是一组抽象的机房数字，而是一批极其昂贵、同时可能产生长期租金收入的基础设施资产。
所以，NVDA财报真正替SPCX验证的不是“GPU还能卖多少”，而是：

SpaceX豪赌的算力，可能真的有人租，而且租金正在变成收入。

我现在的判断：

英伟达没有证明那5GW属于SpaceX，但SpaceX很可能是这份NVDA财报最被忽视的映射受益者。

关注我，我会继续追踪这5GW最后到底属于谁。
非投资建议。

text:
小时候，一名男孩逃课回家，偏偏在路上撞见了父亲。

父亲问他为什么没去上学。

他一紧张，张嘴就编了个理由：

“学校塌了。”

没想到父亲听完脸都变了。

因为父亲小时候，那所学校还真的塌过一次。那次事故留下的阴影太深，所以他几乎没怀疑，立刻给村委会打电话，让人赶紧去学校救人。

消息很快传开。

刚下班的家长们一听“学校塌了”，全慌了，电话一个接一个往学校打，没多久连电话线都快被打爆。

大家越打越觉得是真的。

没人愿意等消息。

骑摩托的、开车的、骑自行车的，全往学校赶。有些家长嫌自行车太慢，骑到一半直接把车一扔，撒腿就跑。

那一天，男孩第一次见识到：

一个逃课的小学生，究竟能调动多大的社会资源。

最后全村都快冲到学校门口了。

而他站在人群后面，脑子里只剩下一个问题：

现在回去上课，还来得及吗？

text:
Woo hoo! Thrilled to announce YouSpot, the AI-native Solo CRM from HubSpot Next.

tl;dr: YouSpot is a CRM built for one-person companies. It builds a "second brain" from your business context and remembers the things you might otherwise miss. We’re launching with an intro price of $1/month for the first 1,000 customers (154 slots already taken). Sign up at YouSpot .com (yes, I'm still paranoid about embedding links in posts even though that's not supposed to matter now).  
—
I’ve thought about this multiple times over the years, and even came close to kicking off a project, but the timing wasn’t right, and the technology wasn’t ready.

Now, the timing is perfect and AI actually works.

YouSpot is a CRM you don’t have to maintain. It's built exclusively for 1 person companies. Solopreneurs, consultants, speakers, writers, creators, etc. It's *not* for GTM teams (I recommend HubSpot). It's also *not* for consumers. It's for operators running a 1 person business. 

You connect Gmail, Google Calendar, LinkedIn, X/Twitter and the other tools you already use.

YouSpot builds the context for you - who you know, what you’ve talked about, what might need a follow-up, and which opportunities may deserve your attention.

It can surface the relationships, follow-ups, and opportunities that matter instead of waiting for you to remember to update a record or create a task.

Here’s what you need to know:

1. YouSpot is part of HubSpot Next, an innovation group inside HubSpot (the #1 agentic customer platform with over 300,000 customers [NYSE:HUBS]).

2. It’s built specifically for the solo market. If your business has a GTM team, even a small one - go with HubSpot. If you’re a 1-person team looking for something more powerful than Claude + a spreadsheet but less weighty than a full CRM, check out YouSpot.

3. YouSpot is truly AI-native. Under the hood, it’s actually implemented as an AI harness with CRM tools inside. You use it like ChatGPT or Claude, but it has structured customer context and tools that let it do much more than just answer questions and respond to prompts.

4. It builds itself from the tools you already use. No spending Sunday night updating the CRM.

5. It doesn’t just store your context. It uses that context to help you figure out what deserves your attention.

6. You can chat with your second brain inside YouSpot – or you can use the robust MCP connector and connect it to ChatGPT, Claude or any AI app that supports MCP.

7. YouSpot supports cloud agents, inspired by OpenClaw. These are “always working” agents that have access to your second brain and can do things on your behalf. You define what you want your agent to do in natural language.

8. The pricing is Pay-As-You-Go. No big commitment. Introductory price of $1/month (that’s as low as I could make it and still let people put it on a credit card).

The product is still early. I built it for myself (outside of HubSpot, I have a small LLC that I use for my indie startup investments and hobbyist domain name investments).  If you’re a solopreneur, would love to learn how you keep track of the people, follow-ups and opportunities that matter today.

And as I like to do, I”m building this in public. I’m making daily updates to the product. Responding to questions and feedback as fast and furious as I can. 

This has been an amazingly fun product to work on. I’m up late night till 2am every night.

Thanks for your interest and support.

All replies read. Even ones from bots and agents.

text:
Anthropic published The AI-Native SDLC Playbook last week saying, “code is no longer the bottleneck.” I agree.

All year long, I’ve been asking myself the questions that naturally follow:

What becomes the bottleneck next?

If models can generate code faster and faster, what actually determines whether a change is good enough to ship?

If teams are going to use multiple models and agents, what has to remain durable underneath them?

And as agents become more autonomous, how do people understand and steer what hundreds of them are doing at once?

My view: faster code generation is already exposing the next constraints. Solving them is where the next wave of value in agentic engineering will come from.

Verification, context, execution infrastructure and governance start to matter more than model choice.

Put differently: when implementation becomes abundant, trust becomes scarce.

I wrote down my view of what comes next: When Code Is Abundant

https://t.co/Dh4j2TIsJr

“正常。”

I'm finally allowed to talk about it! 

I was part of the team behind latest Rsync release, using Proof to perform the full continuous audit on it. 

Rsync ships on virtually every Linux system and has moved the world's files since 1996. It is one of the most used software out there. 

A few months ago, before offering my help to the project I thought - "It's a backup tool, which moving some files. How complex can it be?". How I was wrong.

What I remember most, though, is the queue! 

By our internal count, a few hundred security reports and candidate findings passed through the release cycle. Proof formally filed 99. We later withdrew 28. The release shipped with 33 security fixes.

A convincing security report can now be generated in minutes. On a thirty-year-old project, deciding whether it is real can take hours. You have to recover the threat model, the old compatibility rule, and the reason a strange branch still exists.

Sometimes it is a vulnerability. Sometimes it is nonsense. You cannot know until someone with enough project history does the work.

I wrote about what that felt like from inside rsync: the pressure on maintainers, the limits of generic LLM review, the findings we got wrong, and why the most valuable result was not another report, but a test that stays with the project.

What it feels inside rsync release process https://t.co/aGiDGqsooc

Proof case study: https://t.co/EA3zbHBh2D

text:
The explosive growth of Conductor at Netflix and across at the industry is something I still find incredible.  Read more about this in Netflix Tech Blog by the Conductor Team.  https://t.co/hRQ8rNCRwF

Conductor started with a relatively simple idea. Make it dramatically easier for developers to build complex distributed applications without having to solve orchestration, state, retries, failures and recovery over and over again.  What happened next was amazing. Millions of workflow executions became billions.  More teams adopted it. More applications were built on it. The use cases became larger and increasingly mission critical.   

And Conductor kept scaling. To me, this is one of the most exciting things about building a platform. You can start by solving one hard problem really well, and developers take it places you never imagined.  And we are at the beginning of an even bigger chapter now.  The world is moving from orchestrating microservices to orchestrating APIs, events, data, infrastructure, LLMs, tools and AI agents. Applications are becoming more distributed, more asynchronous and far more complex.  AI and rise of coding agents is also a tailwind for us. There will be more applications that will built in the next 12 months than in the last 10 years.  Conductor is to the goto platform for building these mission critical apps.  The problem Conductor was created to solve is becoming more important than ever.  That is why we built Orkes.  We took everything we learned building and scaling Conductor at Netflix and are now bringing that platform to companies around the world.  And Conductor OSS (https://t.co/uWGvZnpU66) continues to give developers everywhere the ability to build on the same fundamental architecture.  

From millions to billions of executions at Netflix, and literally trillions across the Conductor ecosystem, to what developers and enterprises are building today,. The biggest chapter for Conductor is still ahead of us.

When we used Pogo to analyze longitudinal, multi year purchase trends for prescription verified GLP-1 users, something in the data surprised us. ⬇️ 

As expected, highly processed snacks are down. Protein and back-to-basics items like pretzels are up. Given that impulse and cravings play less of a role in users’ shopping, it makes sense.

Then, there’s gum and mints. Despite their higher ingredient count and candy-aisle location, they’re up by 10%. What’s going on?

For some users, gum and mints are functioning less like candy and more like symptom management for GLP-1 side-effects.

“When I’ve increased my dosage and feel a little nauseous, I find that mints or even a hard candy will help,” says one GLP-1 user. “I do buy more gum and mints.”

“My mouth gets dry a lot” says another user. “Instead of drinking a lot, I like to chew gum.”

For others, meanwhile, it’s just satisfying: a taste of something sweet that doesn’t make you feel full.

It’s food for thought. Want to learn more about this freshly minted shopper cohort?

Comment POGO below to see a full study.

📢 Call for Contributors!!!

Following the initial release, we’re opening RSI-Exam to the community 🌍🔬

Our goal is to work together to establish a rigorous, evolving standard for measuring Recursive Self-Improvement in AI. Building a benchmark at this scale requires expertise from researchers and practitioners across many fields.

Specifically, there are three ways to contribute:

01 — Research Tasks 🔬
Design challenging, executable research environments that push agents to discover genuine improvements.

02 — Reviews 👀
Help critically evaluate task designs, methods, metrics, and evaluation protocols.

03 — Rollout Audits 🕵️‍♂️
Dive into agent trajectories to understand what works, what fails, and how we can make the benchmark more robust.

📅 Next contribution deadline: September 15, 2026

For more info, please visit https://t.co/6OCfd4mIG0

quotedTweet.text:
With frontier models getting more capable by the month 🚀, everyone is talking about Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI). But how do we actually measure this progress? 🤔

Excited to present RSI-Exam — a benchmark testing whether AI agents can improve an existing method through autonomous, long-horizon experimentation, and, importantly, whether those improvements generalize to hidden data. 

Across 88 executable research tasks spanning 6 domains, the trend is clear: Claude and GPT form the first tier, with a clear gap over the rest of the field. Yet there is still huge room for improvement. 

More importantly, the trajectories tell both stories: agents that discover fundamentally better methods — and agents that spend hours rigorously optimizing the wrong idea. 

Check it out: https://t.co/wUcTebZr5w

result.text:
With frontier models getting more capable by the month 🚀, everyone is talking about Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI). But how do we actually measure this progress? 🤔

Excited to present RSI-Exam — a benchmark testing whether AI agents can improve an existing method through autonomous, long-horizon experimentation, and, importantly, whether those improvements generalize to hidden data. 

Across 88 executable research tasks spanning 6 domains, the trend is clear: Claude and GPT form the first tier, with a clear gap over the rest of the field. Yet there is still huge room for improvement. 

More importantly, the trajectories tell both stories: agents that discover fundamentally better methods — and agents that spend hours rigorously optimizing the wrong idea.

text: Had an amazing roundtable meeting with Mr. Mohan Bhagwat in NY. He fielded important questions by all of us from various industries, including telecommunications, space, clean energy, not so clean energy, technology, quantum computing etc. Of course he never speaks on behalf of the Indian government ever..  all of us wanted to know how he could help us at various state level to streamline procedures so that we could set up companies or manufacturing plants in India without bureaucratic drag. He answered brilliantly and inspired confidence in all of us that he might be able to get a few things done.  Few takeaways: the man has a heart of gold, truly believes in a unified India and a unified world, he sees absolutely no difference between various religious groups.  For him all Indians are “Kutumbhakam”.  Family.  Does he have a bias towards any particular group? Yes he does - INDIAN YOUTH.  It was clear to see that he has unshakable confidence in Indian youth, and believes in the change that they are demanding.  He seems to be their biggest champion in the country.  Lucky for India.. 🇮🇳 🇺🇸.  I have come away from the meeting 100% bullish that the Indian youth will drive change in unprecedented ways.  And RSS will help them overthrow the last vestiges of colonial structures that keep India slow.  Proud of my home country 🇮🇳🇮🇳.   What does Mr. Bhagwat think of US ? He’s a true believer in US India friendship and bridge building.. and has promised us that he will visit us more often.  🇺🇸🇮🇳🇺🇸🇮🇳🇺🇸

text:
People in Bitcoin say "don't trust, verify" like it's a bumper sticker. But unless you're a developer, how many of us have actually verified anything about Bitcoin's most important claims or even know what github is?

I hadn't, honestly. So I built a lab for both of us.

It's a fun interactive site that walks you through the claims — the 21M supply cap (it's in the code, you can read it), immutability (you get to try to hack the chain and watch it fail), the seed-phrase math (2048^12 is a number with 39 digits), the difficulty adjustment (drag a slider and watch the network re-balance itself), and more.

No tech background needed. It's built so a kid could use it — and so a skeptic can't weasel out of the evidence.

Every experiment includes a "verify with AI" prompt, because the whole point is teaching you to check things yourself — including this site.

The future isn't trusting the right people. It's not needing to. Let me know what you think!

https://t.co/O7cSpWIDk3
